title: Hopi father and the Schultz family
summary: Dance asks about the Indian side; Edison explains his father's Hopi heritage, his mother's German-named Schultz family and Schultztown.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I want to come back to that Indian thing
because, you know, it's amazing how many -- everybody talks about jazz as the Negro -- but there's a tremendous Indian thing. Did you know Duke was part Indian?
No kidding? No, I didn't know that.
Never said much about anything else.

Yeah, well, it comes out in later years because people get inquisitive. You know, they want to know your past, your bloodline, your roots. So my mother's folks were named Schultz, S-c-h-u-l-t-z, and that's certainly not a name that's befitting to the blacks, you know, Schultz.

German, yeah. And they were all mixed up, you know. In fact, there was a little city in Kentucky, there were so many Schultzs there they named it Schultztown. That was my mother's parents. And during that span of time in Kentucky, my uncle was a coal miner and a farmer, you know. Everything that we ate, everything that we accumulated, so far as the house was concerned, was grown, you know. And I worked so hard there, Stanley, I swore when I went to be a man I'd never work again.
